sporsmal.tekst: A <ul> has the listener ul.addEventListener("click", e => console.log(e.target, e.currentTarget)). The user clicks an <li> inside the list. What is logged?
sporsmal.begrunnelse: event.target is the element where the event started (the <li>), and event.currentTarget is the element the listener is attached to (the <ul>). The event reaches the <ul> by bubbling.

alternativer.tekst: Both are the <ul>
target is the <li>, currentTarget is the <ul>
target is the <ul>, currentTarget is the <li>

sporsmal.tekst: A page has four elements with class item. A script runs const live = document.getElementsByClassName("item"); const snap = document.querySelectorAll(".item"); and then appends a fifth element with class item. What is true now?
sporsmal.begrunnelse: getElementsByClassName returns a live HTMLCollection that updates when the document changes, while querySelectorAll returns a static NodeList.

alternativer.tekst: Both live.length and snap.length are 5
snap.length is 5 and live.length is still 4
live.length is 5 and snap.length is still 4

sporsmal.tekst: A comment box shows user text with el.innerHTML = comment. A user enters . What happens, and what is the fix?
sporsmal.begrunnelse: innerHTML treats the string as HTML, so the onerror code may run. This is XSS, and the notes say to use textContent for text from users.

alternativer.tekst: The onerror code can run (XSS); use textContent instead
Nothing happens, because only <script> tags can run code
The text is shown as plain text, and textContent would make the code run

sporsmal.tekst: app.js needs the DOM and must run after library.js. Both scripts are in <head>. Which setup fits best?
sporsmal.begrunnelse: defer runs the scripts after the whole document has been parsed, in the order they appear. async runs in any order, and a script without attributes in <head> runs before the body exists.

alternativer.tekst: defer on both scripts, with library.js first
async on both scripts, with library.js first
async on library.js and no attribute on app.js

sporsmal.tekst: A script in <head> without defer runs document.getElementById("menu").classList.add("open"). The menu is in the body. What happens?
sporsmal.begrunnelse: The script runs before the body has been parsed, so getElementById returns null. Using classList on null throws an error.

alternativer.tekst: It works, because getElementById waits until the element has been parsed
getElementById returns null, and using classList on null throws an error
Nothing happens and no error is thrown, because an empty result is ignored

sporsmal.tekst: <head> contains <script async src="analytics.js"> and <script defer src="app.js">. Which statement is correct?
sporsmal.begrunnelse: A deferred script runs after the whole document has been parsed. An async script runs as soon as it is ready, which can be before parsing is finished.

alternativer.tekst: Both scripts wait until the whole document has been parsed
analytics.js always runs after app.js, because defer has priority
app.js runs after parsing, while analytics.js may run before parsing is finished

sporsmal.tekst: A link has a click handler that only calls event.stopPropagation(). What happens when the link is clicked?
sporsmal.begrunnelse: stopPropagation only stops the bubbling. The default action, following the link, is stopped only by preventDefault.

alternativer.tekst: The link is not followed, and the event does not bubble
The link is not followed, but the event still bubbles
The link is still followed, but listeners on parent elements do not get the event

sporsmal.tekst: A submit handler on a form calls fetch to send the data but never calls event.preventDefault(). What is the problem?
sporsmal.begrunnelse: Without preventDefault, the browser's default action still happens: the form is submitted and the page reloads.

alternativer.tekst: The handler never runs, because submit fires on the button
The browser still submits the form the normal way and reloads the page
fetch cancels the default submit by itself, so there is no problem

sporsmal.tekst: On page load, a script adds a click listener to each <li> with forEach. Items added later with append do not react to clicks. What is the best fix?
sporsmal.begrunnelse: With event delegation, one listener on the list checks event.target. It works for items added later, because their events bubble up to the list.

alternativer.tekst: Put one listener on the list and check event.target
Use getElementsByClassName, since a live collection gives new items the listeners
Call event.stopPropagation() in each item's handler

sporsmal.tekst: A game should react when the user presses the arrow keys anywhere on the page. Which listener fits best?
sporsmal.begrunnelse: keydown fires when a key is pressed. input and change are about the value of form fields changing, not key presses on the page.

alternativer.tekst: document.addEventListener("input", handler)
document.addEventListener("keydown", handler)
document.addEventListener("change", handler)

sporsmal.tekst: A form contains <input id="email"> and <input name="age">. What does new FormData(form) collect?
sporsmal.begrunnelse: FormData collects all fields that have a name attribute. The email field only has an id, so it is left out.

alternativer.tekst: Both fields, with the email field stored under its id
No fields, because FormData only works inside a submit handler
Only the age field

sporsmal.tekst: Which line removes the element with id old from the DOM tree?
sporsmal.begrunnelse: element.remove() takes the element out of the tree. Emptying its text or hiding it with a style leaves the element in the tree.

alternativer.tekst: document.getElementById("old").remove()
document.getElementById("old").textContent = ""
document.getElementById("old").style.display = "none"

sporsmal.tekst: A script runs el.textContent = "Hi". What does the user see?
sporsmal.begrunnelse: textContent sets the text of the element. The string is not treated as HTML, so the tags are shown as text.

alternativer.tekst: The word Hi in bold
Nothing, because textContent rejects strings with HTML
The literal text Hi

sporsmal.tekst: After a failed form submit, a script shows an error message in a <div>. What best helps both keyboard and screen reader users?
sporsmal.begrunnelse: The notes recommend an aria-live="polite" region so screen readers announce the update, and moving focus to the error with element.focus() so keyboard users know what happened.

alternativer.tekst: Only add a red class with classList so the message is easy to see
Put the message in an aria-live="polite" region and move focus to it with element.focus()
Move focus to the submit button so the user can try again at once

sporsmal.tekst: A script adds 1000 rows. Version A calls list.append(row) for each row. Version B appends the rows to a DocumentFragment and then appends the fragment to the list. Which is correct?
sporsmal.begrunnelse: Each change to the DOM can make the browser recalculate the layout. Version B changes the page only once.

alternativer.tekst: B is faster, because the page is changed once instead of 1000 times
A is faster, because each row appears on screen right away
They are equally fast, because a fragment is inserted one row at a time anyway

sporsmal.tekst: A menu should open on one click and close on the next. Which line in the click handler does this?
sporsmal.begrunnelse: classList.toggle adds the class if it is missing and removes it if it is there. add only opens, and setAttribute replaces all classes.

alternativer.tekst: menu.classList.toggle("open")
menu.classList.add("open")
menu.setAttribute("class", "open")

sporsmal.tekst:
The page has
, and both elements have a click listener. The user clicks the button. What happens?
sporsmal.begrunnelse: The event fires on the element where it started and then bubbles up through the parents, so the inner listener runs first and then the outer one.

alternativer.tekst: The outer listener runs first, then the inner one
Only the inner listener runs, because an event fires on one element
The inner listener runs first, then the outer one

sporsmal.tekst: In the same setup with an outer <div> and an inner button, the inner listener calls event.preventDefault(). Does the outer listener still run?
sporsmal.begrunnelse: preventDefault only stops the browser's default action. The bubbling is stopped only by stopPropagation.

alternativer.tekst: No, because preventDefault also stops the bubbling
Yes, because preventDefault does not stop the bubbling
No, because preventDefault removes the listeners on the parents

sporsmal.tekst: An element has class="card active". What do el.classList.contains("active") and el.getAttribute("class") === "active" give?
sporsmal.begrunnelse: classList.contains checks for one class among several. getAttribute returns the whole attribute value, "card active", which is not equal to "active".

alternativer.tekst: Both give true
Both give false
contains gives true, and the getAttribute comparison gives false

sporsmal.tekst: Which task needs querySelector or querySelectorAll rather than getElementById or getElementsByClassName?
sporsmal.begrunnelse: querySelector accepts any CSS selector, such as nav a.active. Finding by id or by one class can also be done with the older methods.

alternativer.tekst: Finding the first <a> with class active inside a <nav>
Finding the element with id menu
Finding all elements with class card

sporsmal.tekst: A student removes a banner with element.remove() and says: "The banner is now gone from index.html." What is correct?
sporsmal.begrunnelse: When a script changes the DOM, the source file stays the same. The banner is only gone from the DOM, so it comes back when the page is reloaded.

alternativer.tekst: It is removed from index.html until the server is restarted
It is only hidden with display: none and is still in the DOM tree
It is only gone from the DOM; index.html is unchanged, so the banner is back after a reload

sporsmal.tekst: A search form has an input and a <button>. The developer adds a click listener on the button that calls preventDefault and sends the data with fetch. What fits the notes better?
sporsmal.begrunnelse: The submit event fires on the <form>, not on the button. Listening for submit on the form and calling preventDefault there lets the script send the data with fetch.

alternativer.tekst: Listen for change on the button instead
Listen for input on the form and send the data on every keystroke
Listen for submit on the <form> and call preventDefault there

sporsmal.tekst: A sign-up form should check if a username is free when the user leaves the field after editing it, and show a character counter that updates on each keystroke. Which events fit?
sporsmal.begrunnelse: change fires when the user leaves the field after changing it, which fits the username check. input fires on every keystroke, which fits the counter.

alternativer.tekst: input for both
change for the username check and input for the counter
input for the username check and change for the counter

sporsmal.tekst: A page has four elements with class card. A script runs const cards = document.getElementsByClassName("card"); for (let i = 0; i < cards.length; i++) { cards[i].classList.remove("card"); }. What happens?
sporsmal.begrunnelse: The HTMLCollection is live, so each element drops out of it when it loses the class. The indexes shift, and only the first and third card are changed.

alternativer.tekst: All four cards lose the class
Only the first and third card lose the class, because the live collection shrinks during the loop
An error is thrown, because the collection cannot change during a loop

sporsmal.tekst:
Given

Hi you

, what do p.textContent and p.innerHTML return?
sporsmal.begrunnelse: textContent gives the text of the element without tags, while innerHTML gives the HTML inside it.

alternativer.tekst: textContent gives "Hi you", and innerHTML gives "Hi you"
Both give "Hi you"
textContent gives "Hi you", and innerHTML gives "Hi you"

sporsmal.tekst: A script runs const p = document.createElement("p"); p.textContent = "Saved"; but the text never shows up. What is the most likely cause?
sporsmal.begrunnelse: createElement makes an element that is not yet part of the page. It must be inserted with for example append before it is shown.

alternativer.tekst: textContent does not work on new elements, so innerHTML is needed
The element was never inserted into the page with for example append
createElement only works in scripts with defer

sporsmal.tekst: A delegated click listener on <ul id="todo"> runs event.currentTarget.remove(). What is removed when the user clicks an item?
sporsmal.begrunnelse: currentTarget is the element the listener is attached to, which is the <ul>. To remove the clicked item, the handler should use event.target.

alternativer.tekst: The whole list, because currentTarget is the <ul>
Only the clicked <li>
Nothing, because currentTarget is null in delegated listeners

sporsmal.tekst: An element has class="card". A script runs el.setAttribute("class", "active"). What is the result?
sporsmal.begrunnelse: setAttribute replaces the whole class attribute, so card is lost. classList.add("active") would have kept both classes.

alternativer.tekst: The element has both card and active
An error is thrown, because classes can only be changed with classList
The class attribute becomes only active, so card is lost

sporsmal.tekst: <head> contains <script defer src="a.js">, and the end of <body> contains <script src="b.js"> with no attributes. Which script runs first?
sporsmal.begrunnelse: A normal script runs when the parser reaches it, while a deferred script waits until the whole document has been parsed. b.js is reached before parsing is done.

alternativer.tekst: a.js, because it comes first and defer keeps the order
b.js, because a.js waits until the whole document has been parsed
They run at the same time, because both are downloaded in parallel

sporsmal.tekst: In form.addEventListener("submit", e => { ... }), which element is e.currentTarget when the user clicks the submit button?
sporsmal.begrunnelse: currentTarget is the element the listener is attached to. The listener is on the form, and the submit event fires on the form, not on the button.

alternativer.tekst: The <form> element
The submit button that was clicked
The document
